summary_paragraph: The patient, a woman with T1-T2 paraplegia and a history of COPD and recurrent pneumonias, was admitted for sudden onset shortness of breath and increased oxygen requirement. A chest X-ray revealed a right lower lobe opacity consistent with pneumonia, prompting treatment with IV antibiotics, later transitioned to oral Bactrim for completion at home. She remained afebrile and stable throughout her stay, with improving oxygenation. During evaluation, she was also diagnosed with symptomatic yeast vaginitis, likely triggered by recent antibiotic use, and treated with fluconazole. She was discharged home with home health services, oral antibiotics, and instructions to follow up on pending sputum and yeast culture results.
